identity.title: Wide Neural Networks Trained with Weight Decay Provably Exhibit Neural Collapse

problem.claim: Explain neural collapse in end-to-end training of DNNs whose final component contains at least two linear layers.

gap.claim: Prior theory largely used unconstrained features, whose data-agnostic formulation may not capture DNN training.

contributions.claim: Derives generic neural-collapse guarantees from low training error, balanced linear layers, and bounded feature conditioning.
Shows that weight-decay gradient descent provides these assumptions under width, near-optimality, or large-learning-rate stability conditions.
Claims the first demonstration of neural collapse for end-to-end DNN training.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their analysis by moving beyond unconstrained features to end-to-end DNNs with at least two terminal linear layers, and claim the first corresponding neural-collapse result.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report low training error and balancedness for gradient descent with weight decay when the first layer is wide.
The authors report bounded feature conditioning additionally for solutions that are nearly optimal or stable under large learning rates.
Under the stated assumptions, the authors report guarantees for within-class variability collapse, class-mean orthogonality, and alignment with weight matrices.

narrative_sequence.summary: Neural collapse is described as a consistent last-layer geometric representation of training data at convergence.
Existing theory mostly studies unconstrained features, which are data-agnostic and may not reflect DNN training.
The work studies DNNs ending in at least two linear layers instead of unconstrained features.
Generic collapse guarantees are established from error, balancedness, and conditioning assumptions, then connected to weight-decay gradient descent under specified conditions.
The authors claim these results provide the first neural-collapse result for end-to-end DNN training.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates generic guarantees from a second step showing when their assumptions arise during weight-decay training.

lessons.interpretation: This modular structure makes the logical dependencies of a theory claim easier to inspect.
lessons.application: Present a theoretical result in two linked layers: state the conditional guarantee, then identify an optimization regime that establishes each condition.
lessons.exception: This structure is unsuitable when the assumptions cannot be connected to the training procedure or when the work is purely empirical.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact width threshold, convergence requirements, quantitative bounds, or definitions of “nearly optimal” and “stable under large learning rates.”
It does not provide empirical comparisons, proof details, or conditions beyond those summarized in the abstract.
